facts.statement: The genus was originally named Haasia but had to be renamed because that name was already taken by a millipede.
The genus contains only one species, H. gittelmani.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, H. gittelmani

facts.statement: Fossils were found in rocks dating from 100 to 93 million years ago near Ein Yabrud, about 20 km north of Jerusalem.
facts.quote: which was found in Cenomanian to Turonian (Upper Cretaceous, about 100 to 93 million years ago) rocks near Ein Yabrud, in the Palestinian West Bank, approximately 20 km north of Jerusalem

facts.statement: The genus was named in honor of the paleontologist Georg Haas.
facts.quote: It was named in honour of the palaeontologist Georg Haas

facts.statement: Haasiasaurus was one of the oldest known mosasauroids, measuring only 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: Haasiasaurus was one of the oldest mosasauroids, measuring 1 m long.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the genus might be a chimera because the skull and body parts were not found together.
facts.quote: The genus potentially represents a chimera, since the cranial and postcranial material were not found in association.

facts.statement: Haasiasaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
The animal lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Haasiasaurus is an extinct genus of early mosasauroid.
rejected.quote: Haasiasaurus is an extinct genus of early mosasauroid.
